method: Sector score = the average five-pillar composite of that sector's names in the book. Trend compares against last week's average for the same names.

sectors.name: AI hardware & networking
sectors.note: Dell broke out +15.81%% during the week to a 52-week high on a record $95.0bn AI-server backlog, closing at 524.14; Arista rode the same bid, +1.22%% Friday.

sectors.name: Financials
sectors.note: The +162k August payroll print pushed the 2-year to a fresh 52-week high of 4.374%% and the 5-year to 4.545%%, which is directly accretive to net interest income; JPM still eased 0.94%% on Friday.

sectors.name: Energy
sectors.note: Brent finished the week near $95.73, up more than 8%%, with Hormuz throughput down 77%% from Q4 2025 - yet energy equities fell 0.98%% on Friday, the third-worst sector.

sectors.name: Semiconductors
sectors.note: Best sector of the week by a distance: MU +6.1%% and AMD +4.69%% on Friday alone while the S&P fell 0.38%%, and Broadcom's Sep 2 print showed AI semiconductor revenue of $16.7bn, +221%% y/y.

sectors.name: Industrials
sectors.note: Industrials was one of only three advancing S&P sectors on Friday (+0.22%%); Deere made its 25th 52-week high in twelve months and Eaton rose 3.46%%.

sectors.name: Software / AI
sectors.note: The most rate-damaged group: Microsoft lost the $500 handle (-2.04%%), ServiceNow fell 2.97%%, Palantir 4.49%% and Zscaler 4.5%% despite eight price-target raises.

sectors.name: Consumer / LatAm
sectors.note: Consumer discretionary was Friday's worst sector at -1.26%%; Lululemon collapsed 17.38%% on a guidance cut and the 2-year at a 52-week high pressured the LatAm names on currency.

sectors.name: Healthcare
sectors.note: Healthcare was Friday's second-worst sector at -1.04%%, but Boston Scientific rose 1.81%% against it on the back of a four-insider, $9.49m cluster buy at $48.26.

sectors.name: AI power / nuclear
sectors.note: First real sign of life in weeks: Constellation rose 4.88%% and Vistra 3.52%% on Friday as utilities eked out +0.12%%, though GE Vernova (+0.01%%) and Cameco (+0.12%%) sat the bounce out.
